end.summary:
Aditya identified a ball as a sphere and a candle as a cylinder.
They practised identifying cylinders by their curved surface and two flat faces.
They discussed that turning or lying down does not change a shape’s name.
They were not yet consistent when identifying an inverted cone; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Aditya practised naming 3D shapes in toys and everyday objects. They used the cylinder’s curved surface and two flat faces to identify a candle, and later accepted that an upside-down cone is still a cone; the turning misconception was corrected after it appeared. At home, turn a cup, ball, box, and party hat in different directions and ask Aditya to name each shape without changing its name.
